data.narrative:
Cellares is a Series C biotech company founded by Fabian Gerlinghaus and Omar Kurdi, having raised $350M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public equities (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers in Biotech & Health, with particular focus on 3 same-stage private comparables: Colossal Biosciences ($10.3B), Chai Discovery ($3.8B), and New Limit ($3.1B).

Two methods were triangulated. The Peer-Median approach, applicable given Cellares' stage and sector alignment, yields $3.8B as the median valuation across the three same-stage private comps, with a range of $3.1B to $10.3B. The Stage-Progression method applies a 1.7x multiplier to the $12M proxy of total capital raised, implying $20M valuation; this method captures typical Series C progression mechanics but carries limited weight given early-stage magnitude. Public-Comp Anchoring (using the 8.1x P/S median for the sector) is not applicable, as Cellares' revenue is not disclosed. 

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.9B (median) with low and high bounds of $17M and $4.4B respectively. The substantial dispersion—driven by the 3.3x spread among peer valuations—reflects uncertainty in stage and capital-intensity benchmarking within frontier biotech. Key uncertainties include asset quality relative to Colossal Biosciences' $10.3B valuation and revenue trajectory assumptions embedded in peer comps.
